I'm hesitant to close / dup this though because I don't want to lose track of this issue, especially if 4.7 will be supported in the long term.  A bug like this should really be fixed there sooner then later and with that bug being closed, we might miss fixing it here.  But saying all that, I don't know all the backstory to this particular issue.
- do you know why the commit that fixed this wasn't back ported to 4.7.4?
was deemed "breaking change" since it affects the behavior of the API... since 4.5.1.
But I also see the argument that there are likely no users that depend on the 4.5.1-4.7.4 namespace behavior.
The question is, would client code require any updates if this change were included in the 4.7 line?

I doubt there are any applications that depend on this functionality either way (at least I hope not).  Any proper RDF library (or XML library for RDF/XML) should be working with the full URIs, and not using the prefixes.

That said, ignoring the user-supplied prefixes seems much more likely to cause problems than using them.  I can imagine applications expecting their prefixes to be used, and failing when the auto-generated nsXXX prefixes were used instead.

.  I'd be inclined to want to fix this and then help the folks with 'nsXXX' prefixes fix those prefixes.  That being said I'm not sure of a reliable way to fix prefixes yet, since it gets complicated fast, esp. if the 'nsXXX' prefix is in a triple somewhere.

Back-porting the commit seems fine.  Even with this fix, the user isn't truly in control of the prefixes the repository uses; globally registering a prefix on a first-come-first-serve basis is somewhat leaving things to chance.  As Bethany mentioned, there's no real way to manage or change them once they're in.
I do know that for workshops and demos, this fix would make things *look* better, cosmetically

This issue was noticed by Graham Hukill in a post to the fedora community list: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!msg/fedora-community/Q38vsSiyyu8/VYmz0CLpCAAJ

When one creates a resource via a PUT or POST and includes RDF, any new namespaces are not created correctly - they are given the standard 'ns0XX' prefix.

To reproduce this you can send this RDF via a POST to Fedora:

@prefix pcdm: <http://pcdm.org/models#> .
@prefix xs: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema> .
@prefix foo1: <http://www.example.org/foo1#> .
<> pcdm:hasMember "tree"^^xs:string ;
foo1:foo "Fooo" .

Like so:
$ curl -X POST --data-binary "@body.rdf" -H "Content-Type: text/turtle" http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest

Then:

curl http://localhost:8080/fcrepo/rest/new/object/path

Returns:

@prefix premis: <http://www.loc.gov/premis/rdf/v1#> .
@prefix owl: <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#> .
